articleTitle: The Future Of Electronics In Aviation
abstract: Over the past ten years, the addition of a computer capability to air traffic control has added the dimension of semi-automation to the system. We have yet to "scratch" the surface of the full use of technology in both the-computer and electronics field in airborne and ground control equipments. Future major system pro grams that are under development will be highlighted, such as Discrete Address Beacon Systems, Microwave Landing Systems, Advanced Automation programs, and Wake Vortex Avoidance. These plus others will tie together in the mid-1980's to form a much improved na tional air traffic control system.

articleTitle: Computers In Computed Tomography
abstract: Computed Tomography is presented. Basic theory of CT operation along with typical CT images are presented. The computational system architectures as applied to computed tomography is presented. Three basic com puter configurations are described. These computa tional architectures span four generations of computer tomography systems. The systems described include electronic based CT systems, computer based CT systems, and trends towards real time imaging systems.

articleTitle: The Future Of Transportation
abstract: The future of transportation, influenced by serious energy considerations and potential lifestyle changes, is increasingly becoming a social as well as a technical problem. Alternative transportation ap proaches for low density areas as well as metropolitan centers will present a challenge of keeping an overall economy viable as shifts in travel patterns and modes need to be made. While technical improvements in public transportation and in fuel efficiencies for automobiles will be quite important, economic regula tion and voluntary cooperation will become increasingly important as well. Shifting land use patterns and economic activities are bound to be key elements in transportation impacts in the future.

articleTitle: "Overview Of The Process And Mechanisms Of Technology Transfer And Its Impact On Society"
abstract: The discussion will cover NASA's principal program activities, the technologies required to support them, the transfer process that makes this technology avail able for widespread usage, and the economic benefits that result therefrom. Case histories of several transfer examples will be described using both visual aids and movies. Time will be available for questions.

articleTitle: The Marine Technology Complementing Oceanographic Research At Oregon State University
abstract: The School of Oceanography at Oregon State Uni versity was started in 1954 with $10,000 and a row boat. Today the funding level is $6,200,000 and two oceangoing research vessels. Almost thirty percent of these research dollars are spent to develop, maintain or purchase oceanographic research equipment. This presentation is intended to convey how engineering is being applied to a broad spectrum of oceanic research.

articleTitle: Acoustical Holography In Medical Diagnosis
abstract: Recognized for some years as an invaluable tool in industrial and geophysical applications, acoustical holography is proving to be a viable modality in medical diagnostic procedures. The system clearly delineates portions of the body never observed before through any means, as well as visualization of radiation sensitive areas without risk of harmful effects. Present applications include soft tissue ortho pedics, reconstructive survery of extremities, fetal respiration and heart action studies, trauma including hematoma observation, and general body organ position and behavior. Acoustical holography has a goal the visualization of child anatomy without radiation effects.

articleTitle: Integrated Automotive Electrontc Systems
abstract: The Evolution Of Electronics On The Automobile Has Been Slow And Frustrating For Both Automobile Engineers And The Electronic Manufacturers. This Presentation Discusses In Detail The Reasons For Con Sidering Sophisticated Electronics On The Automobile. Parallels Will Be Drawn To The Evolution Of Similar Technology In Other Sectors Of Business And Compari Sons Made To Determine The Reasons For The Slow Growth On The Automobile. Finally, This Presentation Will Look At Future Trends Covering How And Why The Electronics Technology Will Evolve In The Automobile Industry.

articleTitle: A Comparison Of Constructive Placement Algorithms*
abstract: This paper presents experimental results on four constructive techniques for the placement of modules on a printed wiring or wire-wrap board. The four techniques reported upon are the pair-linking, the cluster development, the minimal-interconnected subgraph, and the stochastic methods. The results indicate that for problems larger than 50 modules cluster-development yields better placements, but at the expense of more computer time.

Is Microprocessor Software Really A Problem?
abstract: The likelihood of success associated with any software project has two main paramaters; the problem complexity and the experience level of the designer/implementers. These factors are important because the lowering costs of microprocessor and memory devices results in a large increase in the number of designs which incorporate these devices. In many cases, these designs are dominated by the cost of their software. The understanding of these two parameters is important to the successful management of the resulting software project.

A Continuing Education Program That Works
abstract: As the title implies, this paper discusses an ongoing continuing education program that has been, and is, extremely successful. This paper will present an analysis of the program. Hopefully, other continuing education programs will benefit from these obser- vations, No attempt will be made to compare other continuing education programs with the one in this paper.

Estimation & Identification Of Bilinear Systems
abstract: In this paper, the state estimation and parameter identification problems for a class of continuous bilinear systems is studied. It is shown that the optimal filter, even for the scalar case, is of infinite dimension and an approximate solution is proposed. The solution method involves the use of a conditional best estimate of the state in the multi plicative term rather than the actual state. The Parameter identification scheme is based on the use of the proposed filter and a maximum likelihood approach. The filter provides the mean and variance information for the likelihood functional which in turn is maximized with respect to the para meters for a given set of observations. In order to simulate the proposed filter on a digital computer a discrete version of the original continuous model is developed, employing the closed form solution to the original Ito differential equation. This closed form solution is not available in all cases and we center our discussion around the scalar case. Computations with simulated data are presented and the effect of sampling time, multiplicative noise, observation noise, and the control are discussed.

articleTitle: Applicatiwof Microprocessors In A Multi-processor System
abstract: A multiple microprocessor (MMP) system can be defined as a system composed of two or more micro processors linked together by a certain system control to share a common memory, while each microprocessor is still capable of individual working with its own private memory. The main properties of a MMP system are simultaneously processing, efficient common memory bus utilization and distributed intelligences. The system control can be realized by time-sharing techniques, hardware logic devices, a central micro processor commander or the combination of the above to control the microprocessor switching, common memory bus accessing and common memory interface buffering. Since most microprocessors are not provided with the capabilities like: 1. bus hold/release output signal generating, 2. bus access granted/denied input control, 3. wait/off state before completing an instruction execution, most of the system controls are burdened with software design such as micro processor switching logic, flag test/set/reset se quence, vectored interrupt servicing, etc. Frequently the microprocessors are forced to enter into halt/ testing loop to wait for common memory accessing before a bus access granted signal is received. Complexity of the software program and inefficiency of its testing loop usually degrades the cost effectiveness of a MMP system. The SC/MP microprocessor (by National Semi conductor), having most of the multi-processor capability, can simplify software complexity when it is implemented in a MMP system. In this paper, several multiple SC/MP microprocessor systems will be proposed. Evaluation of these proposed systems with respect to hardware/software design will be discussed. Application of a MMP system in (a) single program, multiple data (b) multiple programs, single data will be illustrated.

A Research APNEA Monitor Based On Microcomputer Technology
abstract: A method for monitoring the respiratory patterns of the neonate is discussed. The system described consists of a mercury strain gauge interfaced with a commercially available microcomputer system. The computer is programmed to detect episodes of apnea. An historical overview of the problems assocIiated with the detection of apnea is presented initially to demonstrate the evolutionary developm ,ent of the system.

Change Detection Metrics And Mixels (mixed Picture Elements) For Computer Analysis Of Low Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: The computer analysis of low resolution remote sensing imagery such as provided by the LANDSAT I and LANDSAT II satellites presents several basic problems. 1. Resolution elements, which are approximately 80 meters square seldom contain single, identifiable, signatures relevant to land utilization. 2. Picture elements (PIXELS) of mixtures of land usage (MIXELS) often contribute adversely to the success of clustering algorithms and pattern recognition techniques. 3. Since the exact spectral signature (features) of a MIXEL are extremely sensitive to slight displacements of the data, it is difficult to accurately assess changes in basic land usage based on repetitive coverage. This paper discusses several techniques which can be used to find MIXELS and use them in a constructive manner in land use classification. It also presents experimental results obtained from clustering algor ithms for conditions in which MIXELS are both included and excluded from the analysis. In conclusion, the paper suggests several change detection metrics which can be used for gross, low cost screening of LANDSAT data for isolation of regions with changes in land utilization.

A Microcomputer Application For Training The Mentally Retarded
abstract: A microcomputer system is being integrated into a training program for the mentally retarded. The system has been interfaced to an assembly line production situation designed to train mentally retarded individuals to eventually work in a non-sheltered environment. The computer monitors training trends and individual productivity levels. Based on this information, the computer is able to provide immediate feedback to either the supervisor or the trainee relative to progress and training.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Requirements For An Advanced Missile System
abstract: The present basing concepts for the new MX Missile require a backup power source to be carried by each transporter-launcher. This power source must exhibit very high energy density, high efficiency, long service life and capability for recharge. This paper reviews the candidate technologies including flywheel, engine-generators, fuel cells and batteries. This paper also describes the advanced development pregrain sponsored by the Air Force to establish and validate technologies for this important application.

articleTitle: Interference And Motion Artifact In Biopotentials
Are There Biological And Psychological Effects Due To Extra High Voltage Installations?
abstract: This paper reviews the recently aroused interest in the possibility of environmental pollution by EHV installations and whether they have any biological and psychological effects. Recent electrical, medical, and psychological research papers, are reviewed and the results are analyzed. EHV clearances, safety, health hazards, pollution, and energy conservation in bulk power transportation are tabulated and compared.

articleTitle: An Overview Of Automotive Electronics, 1977
abstract: The era of automotive electronics is at hand. From the first auto radio of the thirties to the totally integrated vehicle function of the near future, the growth of automotive electronics has been an example of technology serving utility. Consumer demand for convenience and comfort has created some products while federal and state legislation have created a need for others. Coincident with the potential market, there have been a number of new technologies maturing which offer the automotive electronic designer the tools to produce a cost-effective system which can withstand the rigors of the automotive environment. The challenge of new system concepts generally introduces new variables to be sensed. The quest for cost effective sensors which will survive the automotive environment is still another facet of the continuing challenge of automotive electronics. Therefore, it is the purpose of' this paper to present a brief overview of electronics in the automotive industry, relating to growth of electronics to past, present, and future technology and pressures from both government and consumers.
